title: How to hide cursor in Canva on Mac: a guide for clean presentations
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Canva on Mac: Explained
description: Learn how to hide cursor in Canva on Mac. Discover why there is no native setting and find the best third-party workarounds for clean screen recordings.
intro: There is no native setting in the Canva macOS app to hide your mouse cursor while presenting. You must use third-party macOS utilities to remove the pointer from your screen during recordings.
tldr: Canva lacks a built-in feature to hide the system mouse cursor.
The Magic Cursor setting only removes the blue highlight, not the arrow itself.
Third-party apps like Presentify or Cursorcerer are the standard workarounds for Mac users.
These tools operate at the system level, allowing you to hide the cursor across all applications.

blocks.text: Why you cannot hide the cursor natively in Canva

Many users search for a way to hide their cursor in Canva to create professional screen recordings. It is a common frustration for educators and content creators. The Canva desktop app for macOS functions as a bridge to the web platform. Because of this, it relies on standard web browser behaviors. Web browsers do not have a standard way to suppress the system mouse cursor during a full-screen presentation session.

You might see advice online suggesting you can hide the cursor through the Canva interface. This is almost always a misunderstanding of the Magic Cursor feature. The Magic Cursor is an accessibility tool. It adds a blue circle around your pointer to help viewers follow your movements. You can toggle this in the presentation view. Click the More icon at the bottom right of your screen and select Hide Magic Cursor. This removes the highlight, but the arrow remains.
Using third-party tools to hide your cursor

Since Canva does not offer this control, you need a tool that works at the macOS system level. These applications sit between your hardware and the operating system. They allow you to hide the cursor with a keyboard shortcut or after a period of inactivity. Popular options for Mac users include Presentify, Cursorcerer, and Demo Pro. These are available on the Mac App Store or through developer websites.

When choosing a tool, look for one that supports global hotkeys. You want to be able to hide and show the cursor instantly without leaving your presentation. This is helpful if you need to point at something mid-recording. Always check the system requirements to ensure compatibility with your version of macOS. Most modern utilities support macOS 12 and later.
Steps to manage Magic Cursor settings

If you are struggling with the blue highlight circle, you can manage it easily. This is the only cursor-related setting currently available in the Canva app. Follow these steps to adjust your presentation view.

items: Open your design in the Canva desktop app for Mac.
Click the Present button at the top right of the editor.
Select your preferred presentation mode, such as Presenter View or Standard.
Locate the More icon, represented by three horizontal dots, in the bottom right corner.
Click the icon to open the presentation menu.
Select Hide Magic Cursor to remove the blue circle effect.
Select Show Magic Cursor to bring the highlight back if needed.

blocks.text: Best practices for clean screen recordings

Recording a presentation without a cursor requires preparation. If you use a third-party tool, test your shortcut before you start recording. A common mistake is forgetting to unhide the cursor when you need to navigate to a new slide. Practice your flow to ensure you know exactly when to trigger the hide function.

Consider your audio as well. If you are recording a voiceover, keep your movements intentional. If you cannot hide the cursor, try to keep it steady. Rapid movements are more distracting than a static pointer. If you are using a tool like Presentify, you can also use it to draw on your screen. This can sometimes be a better way to direct attention than moving the mouse.

If your Canva app is lagging while you present, it might not be a cursor issue. High-resolution graphics or too many elements on a page can slow down the editor. If you notice the app freezing, try to clear your cache. You can also check for updates in the Mac App Store. Keeping the app current ensures you have the latest stability improvements.

Another issue is the cursor not responding correctly during screen shares. This often happens if you are using a virtual background or a complex recording setup. Ensure that your screen recording software has permission to capture your display correctly in System Settings. If the problem persists, try using the web version of Canva in a clean browser window.

faq.question: Can I hide the mouse cursor in Canva for Mac?
faq.answer: No, there is no native option in the Canva app to hide the system mouse cursor. You must use a third-party utility to hide the cursor on your Mac.

faq.question: What is the Magic Cursor in Canva?
faq.answer: The Magic Cursor is a feature that adds a blue highlight circle around your mouse pointer. It is designed to help your audience track your movements during a presentation.

faq.question: Does the Magic Cursor hide my mouse arrow?
faq.answer: No, toggling off the Magic Cursor only removes the blue highlight circle. The actual mouse arrow remains visible on the screen.

faq.question: Are there third-party tools to hide the cursor?
faq.answer: Yes, utilities like Presentify or Cursorcerer are commonly used by Mac users to hide the mouse cursor globally across all applications, including Canva.

faq.question: Does the Canva web version allow hiding the cursor?
faq.answer: No, both the desktop app and the web version of Canva behave identically. Neither offers a feature to hide the mouse cursor during presentations.

steps.name: Open your presentation
steps.text: Launch the Canva desktop app and open the project you wish to present.

steps.name: Enter presentation mode
steps.text: Click the Present button located in the top right corner of the editor window.

steps.name: Access the more menu
steps.text: Move your mouse to the bottom right corner of the presentation screen and click the three-dot icon.

steps.name: Toggle Magic Cursor
steps.text: Select Hide Magic Cursor to remove the blue circle highlight from your mouse pointer.

troubleshooting.fix: Ensure you have clicked the More icon and selected Hide Magic Cursor specifically.
Check for updates in the Mac App Store and clear your app cache.

lazur.spoken: Where is the Magic Cursor setting?
lazur.result: Lazur will highlight the More icon in the bottom right corner of your presentation view.
